channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Euro: Overvaluation and energy risks weigh against US Dollar – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Halpenny notes that EUR/USD remains capped near its 200-day moving average at 1.1630 and is 2.5%-3.0% overvalued in the bank’s short-term model.

item.title: AUD/USD Price Forecast: Holds breakout near 0.7100
item.description: The Australian Dollar (AUD) trades almost flat at around 0.7100 against the US Dollar (USD) during the European trading session on Tuesday, but is close to its over two-month high of 0.7130 posted on Monday.

item.title: Dow Jones futures drop as soaring US yields, US-Iran friction rattle markets
item.description: Dow Jones futures fall by 0.25%, trading around 53,410 during European hours on Tuesday. Meanwhile, S&P 500 futures decline 0.52% to near 7,730, and Nasdaq 100 futures slip 0.92%, trading near 29,820.

item.title: United Kingdom: Stagnation with stabilisation signs – Deutsche Bank
item.description: Deutsche Bank’s Chief UK Economist Sanjay Raja notes that while the United Kingdom (UK) economy has exceeded expectations, the labour market remains stagnant, with the jobless rate stuck at 4.9% and payrolled employees falling.

item.title: Gold sticks to losses below $4,400 as USD recovers further from two-month low
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) remains depressed below the $4,400 mark through the first half of the European session on Tuesday, snapping a two-day winning streak amid a broadly firmer US Dollar (USD).

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Fragile recovery tied to US – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank FX analyst Michael Pfister highlights that the Canadian Dollar’s recent weakness contrasts with a fragile recovery in Canada’s real economy.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar declines due to increased risk aversion
item.description: NZD/USD depreciates after two days of losses, trading around 0.5880 during the European hours on Tuesday. The pair depreciates as the US Dollar (USD) holds ground on safe-haven flows amid escalating geopolitical tensions between the US and Iran.

item.title: United States Dollar Index extends recovery from two-month low; trades above 99.50
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY), which tracks the Greenback against a basket of currencies, builds on the overnight goodish rebound from the 99.30 area, or the lowest level since June 5, and gains some follow-through traction on Tuesday.

item.title: GBP/JPY Price Forecast: Pound steadies below the 216.35 resistance area
item.description: The British Pound (GBP) edges higher against the Japanese Yen (JPY) on Tuesday and extends gains for the third consecutive day, despite the mixed UK employment figures seen earlier on the day.

item.title: Australian Dollar: Upside risk targets 0.7150 against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann highlight that AUD/USD strength remains intact after a jump to 0.7129, though overbought conditions should confine intraday moves to a 0.7090–0.7130 band.

item.title: Indian Rupee edges up, higher oil prices to remain key drag
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) edges up against the US Dollar (USD) on Tuesday. The USD/INR ticks lower to near 95.67 after refreshing the three-week high at 95.85 in the opening session. The Indian currency has gained slight strength due to potential Reserve Bank of India (RBI) intervention.

item.title: British Pound: Softer as jobs data cools hikes – ING
item.description: ING’s Chris Turner reports a firmer EUR/GBP after UK labour data, with economist James Smith highlighting a cool jobs market and minimal wage pressures, implying little impetus for Bank of England hikes this year.

item.title: Japanese Yen hits drift closer to the key 160.00 level as risk appetite fades
item.description: The Japanese Yen (JPY) accelerates its decline as the US Dollar (USD) draws support from a sourer market mood, with investors wary of a re-escalation of tensions in the Middle East.

item.title: US Dollar: Carry-supported but rangebound near term – OCBC
item.description: OCBC’s Sim Moh Siong and Christopher Wong highlight that still-attractive US Dollar (USD) carry and softer United States (US) data, which have reduced the odds of a September Fed hike, should keep the Dollar rangebound.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD remains sideways around $65, FOMC takes centre stage
item.description: Silver price (XAG/USD) continues to trade in a limited range at around $65.30 during the European trading session on Tuesday.

item.title: USD/CAD Price Forecast: Consolidates below 1.3900 as bears await 200-SMA breakdown
item.description: The USD/CAD pair struggles to capitalize on the overnight bounce from its lowest level since June 3, around the 1.3845 zone, also representing the 200-day Simple Moving Average (SMA) support, and oscillates in a narrow band on Tuesday.

item.title: Forex Today: Mood sours as Middle East tensions come back under spotlight
item.description: Here is what you need to know on Tuesday, August 18:

item.title: Equities: Stagflation fears weigh on US stocks – Deutsche Bank
item.description: Deutsche Bank strategists note that rising oil prices are reinforcing stagflation concerns and weighing on equities globally.

item.title: Euro holds gains against British Pound as UK unemployment disappoints
item.description: The EUR/GBP cross posts modest gains near 0.8550 during the early European trading hours on Tuesday. The British Pound (GBP) attracts some sellers against the Euro (EUR) following the UK employment data. Traders brace for the ZEW Survey from Germany and the Eurozone later on Tuesday.

item.title: British Pound dips to fresh lows near 1.3520 after mixed UK employment data
item.description: The British Pound (GBP) extends its reversal against the US Dollar (USD) on Tuesday as June’s UK unemployment data fails to convince investors in an already risk-off market, as tensions in the Middle East rise.

item.title: Indian Rupee: RBI inflow strategy recalibrated – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank analysts describe how the Reserve Bank of India’s (RBI) early closure of the FCNR(B) swap window follows strong FX inflows and rising liquidity costs.

item.title: British Pound drops against Yen after UK employment data release
item.description: The British Pound (GBP) faces selling pressure against the Japanese Yen (JPY) after the release of the United Kingdom (UK) labor market data for three months ending in June, dropping to near 215.95.

item.title: Euro: Upside bias needs confirmation above 1.1615 against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann report that EUR/USD briefly broke above major resistance at 1.1610 to 1.1614 before fading, leaving the Euro in a near-term consolidation between 1.1560 and 1.1600.

item.title: United Kingdom Unemployment Rate stays at 4.9% in June vs. 4.8% expected
item.description: The United Kingdom’s (UK) ILO Unemployment Rate stayed at 4.9% in the three months to June after reporting 4.9% in the previous reading, data published by the Office for National Statistics (ONS) showed on Tuesday. The data came in above the market consensus of 4.8%.

item.title: Indonesian Rupiah holds weak footing ahead of looming BI policy decision
item.description: USD/IDR remains in the positive territory after experiencing volatility, trading around 17,900 during the Asian hours on Tuesday. The pair continues to draw support from a weakening Indonesian Rupiah (IDR), driven by cautious domestic sentiment ahead of Bank Indonesia’s (BI) two-day policy meeting.

item.title: Swiss Franc edges lower as US Dollar rebounds, FOMC minutes in focus
item.description: The Swiss Franc (CHF) trades marginally lower against the US Dollar (USD) in the early European trading session on Tuesday, with the USD/CHF pair edging up to near 0.8116.

item.title: Euro declines below 1.1600 on US-Iran war worries
item.description: The EUR/USD pair loses traction to around 1.1575, snapping the three-day winning streak during the early European session on Tuesday. The Euro (EUR) edges lower against the US Dollar (USD) as traders remain cautious about the US-Iran conflict and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Australian Dollar bulls seem hesitant near 0.7100 as USD recovers from two-month low
item.description: The AUD/USD pair turns lower following a modest Asian session uptick on Tuesday, awaiting a break below the 0.7100 mark before extending the previous day's retracement from the highest level since June 5.

item.title: EUR/JPY Price Forecast: Rises to near 185.00 after breaking above 50-day EMA
item.description: EUR/JPY extends its winning streak for the fourth successive day, trading around 184.80 during the Asian hours on Tuesday.

item.title: India Gold price today: Gold falls, according to FXStreet data
item.description: Gold prices fell in India on Tuesday, according to data compiled by FXStreet.
